title: Desingularizing along a strictly standard element
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra and $\pi\in R$ with $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$ and $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$. Let $A\to\Lambda$ and $D\to\Lambda$ be homomorphisms of $R$-algebras with $A$ and $D$ of finite presentation over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Assume (1) $\pi$ (its image in $A$) is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element], and (2) there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$ compatible with the maps to $\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$ induced by $A\to\Lambda$ and $D\to\Lambda$. Then there are an $R$-algebra $B$ of finite presentation, a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $B\to\Lambda$, and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $A\to B$ and $D\to B$ whose composites with $B\to\Lambda$ are the given maps $A\to\Lambda$ and $D\to\Lambda$, such that $H_{D/R}B\subset H_{B/D}$ and $H_{D/R}B\subset H_{B/R}$, where $H_{D/R}$, $H_{B/D}$, $H_{B/R}$ are the singular ideals [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] and $H_{D/R}B$ is the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $H_{D/R}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CT (lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard, line 1812) and its proof (applies Lemma lemma-desingularize)

proof.text: Setup over $D$. Write $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$, $\delta:D\to\Lambda$ for the given maps and $\varphi:A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$ for the map of (2). Since $D$ is of finite presentation, hence of finite type, over the Noetherian ring $R$, $D$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Put $A'=A\otimes_RD$, a $D$-algebra via $d\mapsto1\otimes d$; it is of finite presentation over $D$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1) (with $R'=D$, $S=A$; $A\otimes_RD\cong D\otimes_RA$). Regard $\Lambda$ as a $D$-algebra via $\delta$. The map $\alpha':A'\to\Lambda$, $a\otimes d\mapsto\alpha(a)\delta(d)$, is well defined ($R$-bilinear in $(a,d)$ because $\alpha,\delta$ are $R$-algebra maps) and is a homomorphism of $D$-algebras (universal property of the tensor product of commutative algebras), with $\alpha'(a\otimes1)=\alpha(a)$ and $\alpha'(1\otimes d)=\delta(d)$. We use the image $\pi_D$ of $\pi$ in $D$; its image in $A'$ is $1\otimes\pi_D=\pi_A\otimes1$ ($\pi_A$ the image of $\pi$ in $A$), and its image in $\Lambda$ under $\delta$ is the image of $\pi$ under $R\to\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CT (lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard, lines 1831-1860), first sentence ('We apply Lemma 07CR to D -> A (x)_R D -> Lambda and the image of pi in D'); 'Because D is Noetherian' (later in the proof)

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-desingularize] hold for the Noetherian base ring $D$, the $D$-algebra $\Lambda$, the element $\pi_D\in D$, the $D$-algebra $A'$ of finite presentation and $\alpha':A'\to\Lambda$. (a) $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi_D)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi_D^2)$: $\pi_D$ acts on $\Lambda$ as $\pi$ does, and this is the hypothesis on $\Lambda$. (b) $\pi_A$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ by (1), so its image $\pi_A\otimes1$, which is the image of $\pi_D$ in $A'$, is strictly standard in $A'$ over $D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-base-change] (with $R'=D$). (c) The section: the map $A'\to D/\pi^4D$, $a\otimes d\mapsto\varphi(\bar a)\bar d$ ($\bar a$ the class of $a$ in $A/\pi^4A$, $\bar d$ that of $d$), is a homomorphism of $D$-algebras by the universal property of the tensor product (the composite $A\to A/\pi^4A\xrightarrow{\varphi}D/\pi^4D$ and the reduction $D\to D/\pi^4D$ are $R$-algebra maps); it kills $\pi_D^4A'$ because $\pi_D^4\mapsto0$, so it induces a homomorphism of $D$-algebras $\rho:A'/\pi_D^4A'\to D/\pi_D^4D$. Its composite with $D/\pi^4D\to\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$ (induced by $\delta$) sends the class of $a\otimes d$ to $(\text{image of }\varphi(\bar a))\cdot\overline{\delta(d)}=\overline{\alpha(a)}\,\overline{\delta(d)}=\overline{\alpha'(a\otimes d)}$, using that $\varphi$ is compatible with the maps to $\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$; as the elements $a\otimes d$ generate $A'$ additively, the composite is the map induced by $\alpha'$, which is condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-desingularize].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CT (lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard, lines 1831-1860), second and third sentences ('By Lemma 07CC (lemma-strictly-standard-base-change) we see that pi is strictly standard in A (x)_R D over D. As our section rho we take the map induced by the map in (2)')

proof.text: Applying [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-desingularize] (Stacks 07CR) we obtain a $D$-algebra $B$ of finite presentation and homomorphisms of $D$-algebras $A'\to B\xrightarrow{\beta}\Lambda$ with composite $\alpha'$, such that $\mathfrak aB\subset H_{B/D}$, where $\mathfrak a=\mathrm{Ann}_D(M)$, $M=\mathrm{Ann}_D(\pi_D^2)/\mathrm{Ann}_D(\pi_D)$. Since $R\to D$ and $D\to B$ are of finite presentation, $B$ is of finite presentation over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](2). The maps $A\to B$, $a\mapsto$ image of $a\otimes1$, and $D\to B$, $d\mapsto$ image of $1\otimes d$ (the structure map of $B$), are $R$-algebra homomorphisms, and $\beta$ is an $R$-algebra map with $\beta(\text{image of }a\otimes1)=\alpha'(a\otimes1)=\alpha(a)$ and $\beta(\text{image of }d)=\alpha'(1\otimes d)=\delta(d)$, so the maps are compatible with the maps to $\Lambda$. It remains to prove the two inclusions.

proof.text: Claim: if $\mathfrak q\subset D$ is a prime such that $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$, then $\mathfrak a\not\subset\mathfrak q$. Proof. For $k=1,2$, [lem-weil-pbc-annihilator-element-flat-base-change] applied to the flat map $R\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ and $x=\pi^k$ gives $\mathrm{Ann}_{D_{\mathfrak q}}(\pi^k)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^k)D_{\mathfrak q}$; since $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$ we get $\mathrm{Ann}_{D_{\mathfrak q}}(\pi^2)=\mathrm{Ann}_{D_{\mathfrak q}}(\pi)$. Hence $M_{\mathfrak q}=0$: for $x\in\mathrm{Ann}_D(\pi_D^2)$ the element $x/1\in D_{\mathfrak q}$ is killed by $\pi^2$, hence by $\pi$, so $\pi x/1=0$ and there is $s\in D\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $s\pi_Dx=0$, i.e. $sx\in\mathrm{Ann}_D(\pi_D)$ and the class of $x$ in $M$ maps to $0$ in $M_{\mathfrak q}$. The $D$-module $M$ is finitely generated, being a quotient of the ideal $\mathrm{Ann}_D(\pi_D^2)$ of the Noetherian ring $D$ (Step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], $M_{\mathfrak q}=0$ gives $\mathfrak a=\mathrm{Ann}_D(M)\not\subset\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CT (lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard, lines 1831-1860), fifth to seventh sentences ('For any prime q of D such that D_q is flat over R we have Ann_{D_q}(pi^2)/Ann_{D_q}(pi) = 0 because annihilators of elements commutes with flat base change [Algebra 07T8] ... Because D is Noetherian ... formation of its annihilator commutes with localization. Thus we see that a is not contained in q')

proof.text: If $R\to D$ is smooth at a prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$ (in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]), then $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$: choose $g\in D\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $D_g$ smooth over $R$; then $R\to D_g$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]; $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is the localization of $D_g$ at the prime $\mathfrak qD_g$ (the elements of $D\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $g$ are units in $D_{\mathfrak q}$, and the universal properties of localization identify the two rings), so $D_g\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]; and the composite $R\to D_g\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp].
